description: Speed up the n=4096 cooperative-cluster panel, now 66.7% of the n=4096 time (~31360us) and the largest single per-shape cost in the new best (250a694c, 4394us). The cluster panel_factor_cluster_kernel is single-level UNBLOCKED over its cb columns — it lacks the 2-LEVEL MICRO-PANEL (IB block-WY) restructure that the single-CTA n<=2048 panel already has (the FP32 restructure that cut that panel's serial-column-chain latency ~16%). Add the 2-level IB micro-panel inside the cluster kernel: factor cb in IB-wide sub-blocks, apply each sub-block's reflectors to the rest of the cb panel as a block-WY update, exposing parallelism the per-column cluster.sync chain starves on (profile shows it sync-bound at ~6.25% occupancy, K=16, 32 CTAs/148 SMs at B=2). FP32 panel (TF32 fails the gate). Also sweep more-rows/CTA at smaller K. Keep n<=2048 exactly as parent. Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

Single-level cluster (parent) with per-column residency cluster.sync #1 -> __syncthreads. RUNTIME HANG (eval.py wedged >17min on n=4096 validate, GPU pinned, SIGKILLed). That cluster.sync is load-bearing for cluster progress/coherence; __syncthreads desyncs the cluster. Reverted.

2-level CIB=8 micro-panel inside the V1 cluster panel (cluster-cooperative factor + cross-cluster block-WY apply to far cols), cb=16. n=4096 shape 33396us (min of clean runs) vs parent single-level 31384us -- slight REGRESSION. At cb=16 the parent already batches the trailing dot across all far cols in ONE cross-rank sync/col, so the block-apply ADDS ~3 cluster.syncs/panel rather than removing any; the kernel is latency-bound on cross-CTA syncs at 6.25pct occupancy. Validates clean (22 tests + 3 guards).

Same 2-level cluster but cb=32 (CIB=8, 4 micro-panels/panel). n=4096 33510us. KEY POSITIVE: cb=32 2-level (33510) is 2.3x faster than cb=32 SINGLE-level (76734, brief 13) -- the 2-level removes the quadratic serial-trailing-chain blowup, making a wide cb viable. But still does not beat parent cb=16 (31384). Validates clean.

V2 cluster kernel: SINGLE-CTA micro-panel factor (rank 0 gathers the CIB cols, factors alone with intra-CTA __syncthreads, NO cluster.sync) + cluster block-WY apply. Cuts cross-CTA cluster.sync ~CIB-fold (validates clean). But n=4096 REGRESSED HARD to 49003us (ncu: cluster2 kernel 89pct, 354us/instance vs V1 81us): moving the factor to 1 CTA loses the 16x row-parallel reduction across the cluster and adds gather/scatter DSMEM traffic -- the sync-count win is swamped. The factor MUST stay row-parallel across the cluster.

2-level cluster cb=32 CIB=16 (1 block-apply/panel; HALF the trailing-GEMM launches of cb=16). Validates clean (22 tests + 3 guards incl n=4096 dense+upper+diff_correctness). MEASUREMENT BLOCKED by fleet contention: 4 benchmark runs ALL landed in the bimodal slow regime (shape3=26600us at ~3.4x vs clean 7845; shape6=104300us). Estimating clean shape6 via the shape3 (identical-code) multiplier 26600/7845=3.39 -> ~30760us, roughly parent-equivalent (31384). The 2-level family is at-best parent-equivalent: the cluster is latency-bound on cross-CTA cluster.syncs and the 2-level does NOT cut the sync count (parent already batches the trailing dot into 1 cross-rank sync/col). geomean slow-mode 13413 (contended, NOT comparable to clean 4394).

Built and measured the brief's 2-level micro-panel restructure INSIDE the n=4096 cooperative-cluster panel, 5 committed trials + 1 runtime_error. HEAD=15506fa3 (trial1, clean geomean 4418).

MEASUREMENTS (clean fast-mode unless noted; parent 250a694c = 4394 geomean / 31384us shape6):
- Trial1 cb=16 CIB=8 2-level (cluster-cooperative factor + cross-cluster block-WY apply to far cols): 4418 geomean, shape6 33396us. SLIGHT REGRESSION (+6%).
- Trial2 cb=32 CIB=8 2-level: 4432, shape6 33510us. KEY POSITIVE: cb=32 2-level is 2.3x FASTER than cb=32 SINGLE-level (76734us, brief13) -- the 2-level kills the quadratic serial-trailing blowup, making WIDE cb viable. Still does not beat parent cb=16.
- Trial3 V2 (single-CTA micro-panel factor on rank0 + cluster block-apply, cuts cross-CTA cluster.sync ~CIB-fold): validates clean but shape6 REGRESSED to 49003us (ncu: cluster2 kernel 354us/inst vs V1 81us). Moving the factor to 1 CTA loses the 16x row-parallel reduction across the cluster; the sync-count win is swamped. The factor MUST stay row-parallel.
- Trial4(=runtime_error) parent single-level with the per-column residency cluster.sync(#1) -> __syncthreads: RUNTIME HANG (eval wedged >17min, SIGKILLed). That cluster.sync is load-bearing for cluster progress/DSMEM coherence even at B=2, NOT just B>=96. Reverted.
- Trial5 cb=32 CIB=16 (1 block-apply/panel, HALF the trailing-GEMM launches): validates clean; benchmarked ONLY in a persistent ~3.4x slow-contention regime (4 runs, shape3 rock-stable 26600 vs clean 7845). Clean shape6 estimate via the identical-code shape3 multiplier = 104250/3.39 ~= 30743us -> ROUGHLY PARENT-EQUIVALENT, possibly marginally better. NEEDS a clean fast-mode A/B to confirm (could not obtain one -- fleet saturated the entire brief, 5-9 exclusive runs queued, builds starved, one 10min build timeout).

ROOT-CAUSE FINDING (the brief's hypothesis does not transfer): the cluster panel is latency-bound on CROSS-CTA cluster.syncs at 6.25% occupancy. The brief assumed it does 'IB individual cluster.sync'd column updates' for the trailing that the block-WY apply would collapse -- but the PARENT ALREADY batches the trailing dot across ALL far cols into ONE cross-rank cluster.sync per column. So the 2-level adds block-apply syncs (~3/panel) rather than removing any; the per-column sync chain stays ~3*cb deep. The single-CTA panel's 2-level cut a serial-ARITHMETIC chain (it is compute-bound); the cluster is SYNC-LATENCY-bound, so the same restructure is neutral-to-worse.

OPEN DIRECTIONS for fresh briefs (manager's call):
1. cb=32 CIB=16 needs a CLEAN benchmark -- if it confirms <31384 it is a real (if small) win from halving the launch-bound late-panel trailing GEMMs (brief13 noted 530+362 small GEMM instances at B=2). Cheap to re-measure once the fleet quiets.
2. The trailing TF32 GEMM (~30%, many launch-bound small late-panel GEMMs at B=2) overlapping the next panel's cluster factorization (look-ahead/right-looking) -- BLOCKED for me by the 'stream' substring ban (CUDA Stream concurrency needs the banned word); a CUDA-graph or persistent trailing driver might cut the launch overhead without it.
3. TSQR-style INDEPENDENT row-block factorization (G CTAs, G>>16, ZERO per-column cross-CTA sync, fills the GPU at B=2, combine R-blocks) -- brief13's open direction #1; the ONLY structural way past the 32-CTA / 6.25%-occupancy / cluster.sync-latency wall, since K is hardware-capped at 16 and the residency sync cannot be removed (hangs). This is a DIFFERENT algorithm, not the 2-level.
4. Wider cb still (cb=48/64) on the 2-level: needs MAXCB>32 (kernels assume cb<=32) + SMEM recheck; the 2-level removed the quadratic serial blowup so very wide panels may now pay via far fewer panels/trailing-GEMMs.
